rationale: C13 plausibly supplied a concrete drafting template. Both letters address a Cabinet secretary leaving the executive branch with the prospect of entering the Senate, combine personal reluctance about losing the official with approval of the contemplated Senate service, and present the official's prior legislative and Cabinet experience as preparation for that role. C11 and C17 share resignation-appreciation conventions, but lack the distinctive Cabinet-to-Senate transition.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As a personal matter, of course, I have mingled emotions. You have been a tremendous asset to us in the Cabinet and you will be missed.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Although I do so reluctantly and with deep regret, I acquiesce in your decision... your resignation as Secretary of Agriculture.
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the departure of a valued Cabinet secretary through regret tempered by acceptance of the official's decision.

shared_material.child_excerpt: As a member of the United States Senate, you will add a great deal to the working strength we need...
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I hope sincerely that you will return to the legislative councils of the Nation... next time as a member of the Senate.
shared_material.explanation: Both turn immediately from the Cabinet departure to approving or encouraging service in the Senate.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The vast experience you have gained in private life, as a veteran State Legislator, Governor, and able administrator... qualifies you for legislative judgments
shared_material.parent_excerpt: You came into the Cabinet after broad legislative experience as a member of the House of Representatives.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the official's combination of legislative and Cabinet experience to support the contemplated transition to the Senate.
